Name: Equal1
Description:
The hardest problems are not just bigger workloads. They are different classes of problem: optimization, simulation, materials and cryptography challenges that sit beyond classical compute, no matter how much more of it you add. Quantum exists to solve them.

But quantum will not deliver from the lab. It delivers when it becomes deployable: infrastructure that can be bought, run, scaled and trusted inside high-performance compute environments.

That is why Equal1 exists.

Equal1 brings quantum research, CMOS silicon design and systems engineering together to create something different: quantum computing as deployable rack infrastructure. Not just more performance, but a new form factor, new economics and a system built for the data center.

Already proven over multiple generations of silicon. Equal1 RacQ already shipping to customers, including the European Space Agency.

Not one day. Now.

Name: INFRACHIP
ASCENT+
Description:
Building on previous success, and with an additional EU investment of €10m, ASCENT+ brings together 15 partners to make world-class facilities available and to foster the Nanoelectronics community. ASCENT+ offers an extensive portfolio to access state-of-the-art processing, modelling and data sets, metrology and characterisation, and devices and test structures for Nanoelectronics. As such, it significantly advances the first phase of the open-access programme (ASCENT https://www.ascent.network/) which delivered 100 access projects to researchers from 30 countries across the global research community over the last four years and built a community of over 400 researchers.

ASCENT+ integrates a unique research infrastructure with outstanding credentials. The partners’ facilities at CEA-Leti (FR), Fraunhofer Mikroelekronik (DE), imec (BE), INL (PT/ES) and Tyndall (IE) combine research infrastructure and expertise representing over €2.5 billion of investment and several millennia of accumulated knowledge.

ASCENT+ will grow a first-class research and innovation network through the participation of Silicon Europe Alliance members: DSP Valley (BE), MIDAS (IE), Minalogic (FR) and Silicon Saxony (DE) as well as the SiNANO Institute (FR), reaching out to over 3,700 members.

Giorgos Fagas, ASCENT+ lead and Head of EU Programmes at Tyndall National Institute said “The next era in Nanoelectronics is driven by demonstrations of: (i) quantum advantage using solid-state platforms; (ii) low-power, energy-efficient, high-performance computing based on disruptive devices; and (iii) increased functionality through advanced integration of a diverse range of materials and innovative technologies. ASCENT+ offers an unparalleled access opportunity to users, empowering them to respond to these new problems and to advance knowledge and technology through generating novel results and nurturing talent in their own labs.”

Name: HT Materials Science
Description:
HT Materials Science (HTMS) is the global leader in smart heat transfer fluids for commercial and industrial heating and cooling systems. We help any business with a high heating or cooling demand to make significant energy and carbon savings – from commercial offices and data centres through to manufacturers, pharmaceutical & healthcare facilities and more. 

Our patented MaxwellTM product is a drop-in nanofluid additive that’s proven to enhance the heat transfer of a base fluid by more than 15%. It delivers immediate results (with no costly downtime needed), making HVAC systems instantly more efficient and sustainable. 

MaxwellTM can reduce a company’s energy costs by 12-15% or more and can also increase a system’s capacity. This means businesses can get more out of their existing equipment for longer, as their heating or cooling demands increase. Our technology is already being successfully used by a host of major companies across the US, EMEA and Asia, bringing them enhanced efficiencies, cost savings and lower carbon footprints as a result. 

At HTMS we proudly work with some of the best science and engineering minds in the world, with offices in Dublin, Lecce (Italy) and New York. R&D is at the heart of everything we do, and we’re constantly developing future technologies to help businesses reduce energy consumption and their environmental impact.

Name: MSCA Doctoral Network - STRIKE
Description: STRIKE brings together 12 institutes of academic and non-academic sectors from 8 EU countries with the aim to STRIKE malignant tumors using innovative magnetic nanomaterials. New experimental aspects on design and synthesis of nanostructured magnetic materials are applied to the development of innovative magnetic field-responsive nanotherapeutics for osteosarcoma (OS) combinational therapy. Moreover, the peculiar features of STRIKE nanomaterials are exploited for liquid biopsy using biological samples of BRCA+ breast cancer (BC) patients. The cooperation among outstanding universities, research institutes and industries provides the ESRs with trans-national exchanges and the most innovative research trainings in novel anticancer therapeutic strategies, including in vivo biological evaluation, imaging in OS and early diagnosis in BC. STRIKE will raise excellence in research and training in nanomedicine/precision medicine creating new generation of entrepreneurial and innovative multidisciplinary Early Stage Researchers (ESRs).

Name: NanoCosmos
Description:
The main aim of the NanoCosmos project is to create a European multidisciplinary and intersectorial network to harness the recovery of valuable bioactive compounds from plant by-product matrices for nano-applications in the cosmetics industry. 

The project will ensure (i) exchange of knowledge on bioactive compound properties, (ii) optimization of green extraction processes of such compounds from plant by-product materials, (iii) creation of innovative nanoencapsulated biocomponents for cosmetics formulations, mainly targeted on human sensitive skins. 

NanoCosmos project will aim at enhancing cross fertilization in the area of bioactive compounds from different plant byproduct materials which will result in a more cost-effective use of skills and resources in circular bioeconomy. It will also involve handson practice in different analytical methods in connection with industrial scale-up, performed by both young researchers/PhD students (ESR), experienced researchers (ER) and experienced academics. 

Science and business cooperation will allow the development of a joint research network to address current needs in the area of the cosmetic industry. The project will promote university business dialogue and partnership especially in the context of greater involvement of practitioners in the preparation of ESR career development.

Name: Nanoscale Function Group
Description:
At the Nanoscale Function Group, we are advancing the frontier of nanotechnology by enhancing Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) to go beyond structural imaging—toward functional analysis at the molecular level. Our mission is to unlock the potential of nanoscale science in biological and medical systems, where understanding and manipulating interactions at the single-molecule or single-cell level can pave the way for breakthroughs in disease detection, prevention, treatment, and biomimetic material development.

By actively developing AFM instrumentation and pushing measurement capabilities, we enable researchers to explore complex biological systems under physiological conditions, with unmatched resolution and sensitivity. Our innovations in AFM technology empower fundamental discoveries at the intersection of physics, biology, and engineering.

Name: LirOptic
Description:
LirOptic, headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, is an innovative spin-out from University College Dublin (UCD), born from groundbreaking research in the UCD Physics Department.

Our core technology—solid-state, shapeshifting, and tunable lenses—was developed by Professor Dominic Zerulla and his highly skilled "ultra-fast nano optics" team. The cutting-edge work at UCD laid the foundation for LirOptic’s future in revolutionizing optics and imaging.

The journey from research to industry was further strengthened when Simon Forsyth & Joe O'Keeffe joined Professor Zerulla  to commercialize this breakthrough technology. 

LirOptic has gained significant traction and interest across various industries and the technology is poised to transform Compact Camera module (CCM) lens design for applications ranging from consumer electronics to space and defence - bringing the future of optics into sharper focus.

At LirOptic, we are passionate about pushing the boundaries of what’s possible utilising our technology.

Name: DISCO - DNA  Infrastructure for Storage and COmputation
Description:
Throughout evolution, Biology has found an almost-perfect molecule to pass information down through the millennia. Whether, for a simple bacterium or the largest whale, DNA achieves high information density while permitting cellular machinery rapid random access retrieval to decode everything from a single protein to the development of an entire human brain.

Humanity’s rapidly growing data storage and computing needs make it tempting to exploit optimised biological molecules and processes, but biology is messy, poorly understood and much more specialised for life than it is for our needs — we propose to use DNA for storage together with a rationally designed, well-characterised and robust molecular computing architecture.

Funded by the European Innovation Council (EIC) -  Europe’s flagship innovation programme to identify, develop and scale up breakthrough technologies and game changing innovations - the DISCO project  will address the challenge of engineering a programmable and robust DNA storage and computing platform.

Name: Net4Air
Description:
Net4Air project, run by the National R&D Institute for Microtechnologies in Bucharest, Romania, is a Coordination and Support Action funded by the European Commission under the Twinning framework.
The goals of the Net4Air project are to significantly advance excellence capacity and resources in IMT with a view of addressing the research and innovation gap and imbalance within Europe by broadly increasing IMT expertise, know-how and attractiveness in innovative nanotechnologies, materials, devices, smart systems, data analytics and best-practices for environment monitoring. Project’s goals are in line with the European Green Deal principles for protecting the environment and contributing to citizens health and wellbeing. 
A Networking Centre for excellence in Nanoelectronics was launched within the project by joining together around the Consortium partners and the R&D actors (from research institutes, universities departments, environmental  NGOs, national accredited labs, SMEs, and big industrial players) in Sensing Technologies and Data management for Environmental monitoring applications, to bridge the gap between Western Europe organizations and lower-performing institutions in Romania and therefore making a contribution towards facilitating Romania’s better integration into the European Research Area.

Name: Tuireann Energy Ltd.
Description:
Product: T1 is an innovative fuel additive for gasoline, diesel and ethanol based internal combustion (IC) engines. It consists of T1 Formula, a unique water based low concentration metal nanoparticle fuel additive, and T1 Injector, a specifically designed injector for applying the formula into the engine.

Value proposition: In a world demanding better solutions to global energy and climate changing problems, T1 improves engine efficiency by 10% for gasoline and 8% for diesel on average while simultaneously reducing CO, NOx and Soot emissions. It does this in a very affordable and low impactful manner.

Customers / users: Customers and users of T1 are both IC engine manufacturers and end users.

Business model & commercialisation: T1 will be sold to in-use engines via installers and distributors, while it will be provided to engine manufacturers via a technology licence. The solution will first be adopted by in-use engines due to lower barriers of entry. Once demonstrated and validated in this environment we then expect to get our first licence sales.

Key partnerships secured: Cambustion (UK) & Chalmers University (SE) for vehicle verifications; Coventry University (UK) & Brighton University (UK) for engine analysis; WetSus (NL) & NHL Stenden (NL) for liquid properties analysis; and Brockley (IE) & DIT/CREST (IE) for technical and manufacturing developments; Westward Engineering (IE) &  Lawlors' Automotive Solutions (IE) for vehicle tuning; Recon Waste Managements (UK) for lorry testing; and Hanna-Moore-Curely (IE) for legal advises.
